items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: When I was playing with the Bay Ridley band on the Pelican, I used it up there a while

ctx.x: Do you still play violin or something?

No, I haven't fooled the violin. When I was playing with the Bay Ridley band on the Pelican, I used it up there a while, because I could only read, I mean, play what I see at that time. I didn't learn how to fake much on it. Oh.
What kind of banjo have you got?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: So I think coming back, I think I went back with the Bay Rizzle band.

ctx.x: Around in that neighborhood? The only thing I remember, I remember there was a colored theater and there was one place we used to go, like I used to go eat. And you could drink like, you know, during probation days and get whiskey and things. But, yeah, when this fella Red came on the boat and work, well like I said, I was still around Memphis because I had gotten my hotel room and he and I feel like we were still on a good time. It wasn't long. So we went up with them one night for this particular place. I…
Budweiser? Was it near the Budweiser?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: I stayed with that band until Rebair and his brother fell out

ctx.x: How long did you stay in Pensacola?

Oh, I think it was, let's see, I went there in 24, I must have came around about, no, about 20 years, about three years, about 27 years. I said, well, when the job was closed and we left Pensacola, and one stayed in Mobile, and they had a union there. They had a union in Jacksonville. We didn't have no union, black union in New Orleans. And when I was coming back, I told my daddy, this thing was really getting bad.
